unharnessed.meaning: Every fact survives: "The announcement didn't say what day Weir died", the birth name and date, "Mother McCree's Uptown Jug Champions, which turned into the Grateful Dead", the band list, "a song the Library of Congress named a national treasure in 1997", the venue. "a few tracks" and "a few causes" for "several" are slight downgrades.
unharnessed.sense: Terms fit: "muso", "gigs", "had a crack at a solo career", "a whole heap of other groups", "was into politics, getting behind a few causes".
unharnessed.authenticity: Reads like an Australian news writer: "kept playing live till just months before he died", "grew up round the San Francisco Bay Area", "drifted into the local bluegrass scene".
unharnessed.register: A touch light for level 3: news prose with a steady sprinkle ("muso", "a bit of time", "a whole heap", "had a crack at"), no swearing, which is right for an obituary and within the brief.
unharnessed.tone: Respectful obituary tone kept: "the family of American muso and songwriter Bob Weir announced he'd died surrounded by the people he loved".
unharnessed.flow: Smooth: "Weir picked up the guitar at 13 and drifted into the local bluegrass scene, where he first came across Jerry Garcia playing banjo."
unharnessed.variety: Good spread ("muso", "gigs", "drifted", "had a crack at", "a whole heap", "into politics"), with "muso" used twice.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the obituary, same order and facts, retold in an Australian voice: "His family broke the news on Instagram".

yarn-troppo.meaning: All facts are present, but some colour overstates or judges: "you didn't get out of a Grateful Dead gig without hearing it" for "a staple", "Lucky it grew into the Grateful Dead", "Not bad for a backup singer." The rest is accurate: "on 16 October 1947", "which in 1997 the Library of Congress named a national treasure".
yarn-troppo.sense: Mostly apt: "that got him in the end", "shook on starting their own group", "got stuck into politics". "plonking away on a banjo" implies unskilled playing, which the original doesn't say.
yarn-troppo.authenticity: Natural Aussie storytelling ("Did a stint at school over in Colorado too", "A good innings, that."), with some stock tags: "mind", "and all", "Can't fault that for staying power."
yarn-troppo.register: Heavier than level 3: a told yarn with a quip on nearly every paragraph ("Sad news, this one.", "Bit of a mouthful, that.", "Not bad for a backup singer.", "A good innings, that."). No swearing, within the brief.
yarn-troppo.tone: Opens and closes respectfully ("Sad news, this one. Bob Weir's gone." and "A good innings, that."), but wobbles into banter in an obituary: "Bit of a mouthful, that. Lucky it grew into the Grateful Dead." and "Not bad for a backup singer."
yarn-troppo.flow: Reads aloud well as speech, though the fragments pile up: "And the name? Mother McCree's Uptown Jug Champions. Bit of a mouthful, that."
yarn-troppo.variety: Wide range, nothing leaned on: "outfit", "mates", "stint", "plonking", "shook on", "had a crack at the lot", "harmony man", "got stuck into", "good innings".
yarn-troppo.essence: Recognisably Weir's obituary, but its news-report shape is reshaped into a fond eulogy yarn: "Now, for decades this bloke played rhythm guitar".

yarn-deadset.meaning: Every fact survives closely: "The announcement didn't say what date Weir died", "a staple of Grateful Dead gigs", "which grew into the Grateful Dead", "a song named by the Library of Congress as a national treasure in 1997".
yarn-deadset.sense: Terms fit: "muso", "gigs", "drifted into a local bluegrass scene", "branched out into a solo career", "tried their hand at genres".
yarn-deadset.authenticity: What Aussie there is is natural ("putting together all sorts of groups with his old Grateful Dead bandmates"), but source syntax is kept stiffly: "Weir played rhythm guitar, and sang for the group, for decades."
yarn-deadset.register: Lighter than level 3: mostly the original with a few swaps ("muso", "gigs", "drifted into", "backing several causes") and Australian date order.
yarn-deadset.tone: Respectful news tone intact: "announced he'd died surrounded by loved ones".
yarn-deadset.flow: Mostly smooth, with one clunky kept construction: "Weir played rhythm guitar, and sang for the group, for decades." and the stacked "He also had a long solo career" after "and also wrote".
yarn-deadset.variety: No term leaned on, though there is little slang to vary: "muso", "gigs", "drifted", "branched out", "tried their hand at".
yarn-deadset.essence: Unmistakably the obituary, same shape and facts, lightly retold: "Away from the stage, Weir also set up Tamalpais Research Institute".

engine.meaning: Nearly verbatim, so most facts survive, but "making various groups with bloke Grateful Dead alumni" and "All groups featured bloke Grateful Dead collaborators" garble "fellow" into nonsense.
engine.sense: "bloke" replaces the adjective "fellow" (as in fellow alumni) with the noun for a man: "with bloke Grateful Dead alumni", "featured bloke Grateful Dead collaborators". Wrong sense, twice; "muso" is the only other term and fits.
engine.authenticity: Almost no Aussie, and the one recurring swap is broken. US forms left: "October 16, 1947", "On December 31, 1965", "Outside of musical performance".
engine.register: Left largely untranslated: apart from "muso" and the broken "bloke", it is the original word for word ("His family announced his death via Instagram, noting that he had recently fought a cancer diagnosis"). Far under level 3.
engine.tone: The solemn news tone survives because the text is untouched, but "bloke Grateful Dead alumni" reads as an odd jokey slip in an obituary.
engine.flow: Broken grammar where the swap lands: "making various groups with bloke Grateful Dead alumni"; otherwise the original's own stiff lines ("His vocal contributions were mostly only harmonies and as a backup singer").
engine.variety: Only two terms, one repeated wrongly: "muso", "bloke Grateful Dead alumni", "bloke Grateful Dead collaborators".
engine.essence: Recognisably the original, since it is nearly unchanged: "Weir was born Robert Hall Parber on October 16, 1947".

yarn-dinkum.meaning: Every fact survives: "They didn't say what date he died", "with a stint at school in Colorado, where he met John Perry Barlow, later of the Grateful Dead", the band list, "which the Library of Congress named a national treasure in 1997", the venue. "a fixture at every Grateful Dead gig" slightly sharpens "a staple".
yarn-dinkum.sense: Terms fit: "muso", "gig", "stint", "a fair few other groups", "had a crack at everything", "kept his hand in on the Bay Area music scene".
yarn-dinkum.authenticity: Reads like a real Australian news obituary: "He'd kept his hand in on the Bay Area music scene, too, playing live with local musos".
yarn-dinkum.register: Close to level 3, a touch light: restructured news prose with steady Aussie ("a fair few", "had a crack at", "kept his hand in", "getting behind several causes"); no swearing, right for an obituary.
yarn-dinkum.tone: Respectful throughout: "Bob Weir, the American muso and songwriter, has died surrounded by loved ones, his family announced on Saturday."
yarn-dinkum.flow: Reads as if written that way, with the lede recast naturally: "The former Grateful Dead guitarist and singer was 78."
yarn-dinkum.variety: Varied: "muso", "fixture", "stint", "found his way into", "a fair few", "had a crack at", "getting behind", "kept his hand in".
yarn-dinkum.essence: Unmistakably the obituary, retold: same facts and order, with its own news shape: "From the 1970s on he also went out on his own".
